body.statement: Characterize the exact complexity of \(\mathsf{RSJID}\) when every completion has bidirected degree at most \(d\) at both \(T\) and \(Y\), while the union of possible switched neighborhoods may be unbounded: determine whether a fixed \(d\) preserves \(\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}\)-completeness or yields a polynomial-time or fixed-parameter algorithm.
body.justification: The lower bound controls nonterminal degree but leaves both terminal degrees unbounded.
body.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash show that fixed-graph structure can restore tractability, while Bachtler et al.'s acyclic hardness does not control terminal incidence.
body.consumer: The frontier determines whether sparse completion-wise terminal neighborhoods admit a specialized exact dosearch planner.
